name_reason: Follows data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention: domain=chapter, descriptor encodes chapter 18 + end-scene + per-character facing + data shape (table). The 'ch18' segment is a valid FD2 chapter ID (chapters 01..30) and is meaningful domain context, not a Ghidra address residue (the table address 0x521E5 appears nowhere in the name). The name correctly reflects the data type (a flat read-only byte lookup table) and is byte-identical to the live Ghidra symbol and the src declaration. Consistent with its 8 sibling tables in chtab2.c (ch12/ch14/ch16/ch17/ch18 pos_x/pos_y/facing).
purpose: Per-character sprite facing/direction lookup for the chapter 18 (Distant Shore) end scene; supplies the param_3 facing block that fd2_chapter_18_end hands to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro to orient each placed character's sprite.
logic_summary: Read-only flat uint8[17] of direction codes. fd2_chapter_18_end @ 0x23D0D loads its address (MOV ESI,0x521E5) and copies all 17 bytes onto the on-stack placement block via MOVSD.REP x4 (16 bytes) @ 0x23D12 + MOVSB (1 byte) @ 0x23D14, then passes the stack block as the param_3 facing argument to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro. Because that block address is >= 4, the helper treats param_3 as an array base and indexes it per character: bVar2 = *(byte *)(char_idx + param_3), storing bVar2 into runtime_char.pSprite_state[1] (the sprite facing field) for each char in the placement loop. Stride 1, no element scaling. Live contents: {3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3, 0,0,0, 2,2,2, 1}. Length 17 is established authoritatively by the handler's 17-byte copy (4 dwords + 1 byte); the preceding pos_y_table @ 0x521D4 is the prior MOVSD source and the next analysis byte follows immediately after the 17th element.
element_semantics: Each byte is a per-character sprite facing/direction code in the range 0..3 (the same direction encoding stored into runtime_char.pSprite_state[1]); element index = character placement index used by the chapter-18 end-scene placement loop.
notes: Verified against ground truth: read_memory(0x521E5,17) = [3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,0,0,0,2,2,2,1]; xrefs_to show the sole reader fd2_chapter_18_end (DATA @ 0x23D0D, READ @ 0x23D12) with no writers, confirming const (is_const=true). disassemble_function(fd2_chapter_18_end) confirms the 0x521E5 load + MOVSD.REP x4 + MOVSB 17-byte copy. decompile_function(fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro @ 0x233C6) confirms the param_3<4 fixed-value vs param_3>=4 per-byte-array branch and the store into prVar1->pSprite_state[1]. The src comment block (chtab2.c lines 182-198) is already accurate, ASCII-clean, detailed, and consistent with its sibling facing/pos tables, so it was left untouched (comment_verdict=keep); only the prose 'MOVSB at 0x23D12/0x23D14' is a tiny imprecision (0x23D12 is the MOVSD.REP, 0x23D14 the MOVSB) but the address pair correctly pinpoints both copy instructions and the statement is neither contradictory nor outdated, so no edit was made. The Ghidra data plate at 0x521E5 was empty (PLATE=<null>); per the refine rule for blank plates a concise PLATE_COMMENT was created (ghidra_plate_action=created) via run_script_inline + cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,...), content derived from the src conclusion. Data-quality observation (out of scope, not a logic issue, not acted on): a stray internal Ghidra symbol 'chapter_19_end_event_arg_b' currently sits at 0x521E9, 4 bytes inside this 17-byte table's footprint -- a leftover label that does not affect the src (which declares the full 17-byte array) nor program logic. No equivalence/logic concerns: issues=[].
